_why: This repo has repeatedly carried TWO records asserting DIFFERENT values for the SAME physical parameter, with nothing surfacing the disagreement. Four were found in one day (2026-10-07): a 22x22mm hub outline vs a generated 55x45mm (now 103x103mm) board; a 16MB ESP32-S3 flash claim vs the fitted -N8R8 part's 8MB; '2.4GHz RX on the F33' vs the bare LoRa2021; and a 'horizontal' wing vs the ADR-049 VERTICAL blade. A fifth (the F33 castellation land) had just changed value. A human noticing each one by hand does not scale. This file is the ONE machine-readable list of contested parameters.
_rule: ONE parameter = ONE owning record = ONE canonical value. When a second record is found asserting a different value, add or update an entry HERE (owner, canonical, the conflicting record, and a `forbid` regex) the same day. Do NOT resolve a contradiction by editing the losing record's body: append a CORRECTION block (the repo's convention, see ADR-042/ADR-056) citing this registry, so the history stays legible. `scripts/param_ssot_check.py` is the mechanical enforcement and fails closed; `tests/test_param_ssot.py` proves it fails on a planted contradiction.
_how_annotations_work: A conflicting value found by a `forbid` regex is NOT a failure when it is clearly annotated history rather than a live assertion. A match is allowed if the MATCHED LINE carries a line marker ('was', 'stale', 'superseded', 'guess', 'TODO(unverified)', '->' ...) OR the FILE carries a file marker (an appended 'CORRECTION' block, a citation of docs/ssot/parameters.json, or a statement that the figure is 'inherited'/'RESOLVED'). An UN-annotated conflicting assertion is the defect the gate catches.

parameters.name: ESP32-S3 fitted flash size (the WROOM module on the flight board)
parameters.canonical: 8 MB (ESP32-S3-WROOM-1U-N8R8; in Espressif part numbering N8 = 8 MB flash, R8 = 8 MB PSRAM)
parameters.who_else_asserted: tracker/firmware/sdkconfig.defaults.esp32s3 (header comment) AND the tracked, generated tracker/firmware/sdkconfig AND ADR-029 D1 item 5 all said '16 MB flash' until 2026-10-07 (commit e4d0569). docs/adr/061-onboard-storage.md and docs/analysis/onboard-storage.md carried the correction. A 16 MB flash-size setting on an 8 MB part misplaces the bootloader/application offsets, so this was a live build defect, not a comment.

exempt.reason: The ADR-061 storage audit that FOUND and documented the '16 MB flash' defect (its §Context). It states the corrected 8 MB value itself; it is the finding record, not a live assertion.

forbid.note: a 16 MB flash-size build setting on the 8 MB -N8R8 part
a prose claim that the S3 module has 16 MB flash
a 16 MB figure attached to the WROOM module / PSRAM

parameters.name: Which radio carries the v9 2.4 GHz RX (uplink)
parameters.canonical: 2.4 GHz RX on the bare LoRa2021 (crystal-only); 433 MHz TX on the LoRa2021F33-2G4 (internal 0.5 ppm TCXO)

anchors.regex: one LP on 433 TX, one LP on 2\.4 RX

parameters.who_else_asserted: docs/analysis/external-clock-and-ocxo.md §C1 said the 2.4 GHz path is 'RX on the F33, whose internal 0.5 ppm TCXO gives 1.2 kHz' and concluded 'TCXO-referenced either way'. It was corrected in place on 2026-10-07 by an appended block ('CORRECTION (2026-10-07, appended by ADR-057) — the 2.4 GHz path is NOT F33-referenced'), citing ADR-034 D4 and V9-RADIO-SITE-MATRIX. ADR-034 D1/D4 and the site matrix are the owners.

forbid.regex: 2\.4\s*GHz[\s\S]{0,200}?RX on the F33|RX on the F33[\s\S]{0,200}?2\.4\s*GHz
forbid.note: asserts the 2.4 GHz path is received on the F33, contradicting ADR-034 D4 (bare LoRa2021)

parameters.name: Wing plane orientation at the hub (the ADR-049 wing architecture)
parameters.canonical: VERTICAL wing plane (a blade): long axis radial in the hub plane and pointing outward, 25 mm width vertical. Long axis horizontal/radial — NOT the wing plane horizontal.

anchors.regex: wing plane normal to the hub plane

parameters.who_else_asserted: docs/WING-TO-HUB-SOCKET-SPEC.md §1 says 'Wings 1–2 horizontal, 3–4 inclined ≈30° below the hub plane' and, two sentences earlier, 'the wing's long axis is perpendicular to the hub plane' — self-contradictory within one paragraph. Its derivative carry is docs/adr/048-*.md §5 item 6 / v9 sheet item OPEN-23 ('The footprint therefore asserts no rotation'). The ultimate origin of the 'horizontal' reading is docs/hardware-design.md §3D-Assembly (2026-05-20, v1-era), where 'Wing 1 … horizontal' was an ANTENNA-coverage statement for a wing that carried a Yagi — and ADR-046 §2.4 makes the wing antenna V2-only and absent on v9. ADR-049 §5 item 6 resolves it to VERTICAL by the tab/slot arithmetic (a 9.0 mm tab cannot fit a 6.0 mm in-plane slot; a 0.6 mm tab cannot enter a 0.9 mm in-plane slit), and ADR-046 §4.1 ('90° to the hub plane, wing plane normal to the hub plane'), ADR-051 §1.4 and ADR-055 §1 agree.

forbid.note: says wings 1–2 are horizontal (in the hub plane), i.e. the wing plane is coplanar with the hub — excludes the ADR-049 vertical blade

forbid.regex: long axis is\s*\*{0,2}perpendicular to the hub plane
forbid.note: says the wing's long axis is perpendicular to the hub plane; ADR-049 fixes the long axis RADIAL (in the hub plane)

parameters.name: v9 hub board outline
parameters.canonical: 70.0 x 70.0 mm (the v9 hub board, tracker/hardware/hub_board_v9.kicad_pcb). REVISED 2026-10-14 by measurement from the 60 x 60 mm this ADR first chose; the 60 mm figure came from aggregate courtyard arithmetic, which cannot see that a single 39.65 x 22.30 mm body (U2, LoRa2021F33-2G4) wastes more area than its own footprint implies. Measured with tracker/hardware/seat_probe.py: 60 x 60 overflows U2; 65 x 65 overflows U5 instead (a trap -- it moves the problem); 70 x 70 seats all 39 parts with no overflow and routes 48/48 nets, zero open. See docs/fab/hub-v9/SEAT-PROBE-RESULT.md. The TRUE 103.0 x 103.0 mm S0 placement-stage floorplan -- the array-plane square of ADR-051 2.3 / ADR-055 D5 -- is SUPERSEDED as a board outline: it was never a frozen fab outline.
parameters.who_else_asserted: docs/hardware-design.md:13,21 says '22mm x 22mm' (v1-era, committed 2026-05-20 — the ONLY source of that figure in the whole repo; no generated artifact ever encoded it). docs/adr/055-*.md §3 resolved the inherited outline to 55 × 45 mm on 2026-10-07 (the v8h rectangle). The S0 v9 hub placement then MEASURED and REJECTED 55 × 45 mm (39 footprinted components need 2582 mm² of courtyard against a 2475 mm² board) and set 103.0 × 103.0 mm. docs/adr/040-*.md still says 'the 55 × 45 mm v9 board'. ADR-051 §2.3 and ADR-055 D5 derive the ≈103 mm square as the array area's implied square. || 2026-10-16: the 103.0 x 103.0 mm figure was still the CANONICAL value in this registry while NINE documents and the built board said 70 x 70 mm, and grep found no record that had decided 70 x 70 until ADR-068 was located. The registry was the stale party: ADR-068 (revised 2026-10-14 by measurement, docs/fab/hub-v9/SEAT-PROBE-RESULT.md) is the owner. Found by the test_param_ssot anchor check failing in CI on PR #206.

forbid.note: asserts the hub is 22 × 22 mm (v1-era inherited prose; the current v9 hub is 103 × 103 mm)
asserts the v9 hub board is 55 × 45 mm (the inherited v8h outline, measured and rejected for the v9 hub)

asserts the hub board outline is 103 x 103 mm -- that was the S0 placement-stage floorplan (the array-plane square), SUPERSEDED as an outline by ADR-068 as revised 2026-10-14. The board is 70 x 70 mm.

parameters.name: F33 (LoRa2021F33-2G4) castellated pad land size
parameters.canonical: 1.30 × 1.30 mm (castellation hole diameter D = 0.80 ± 0.10 mm grown by a uniform 0.25 mm solder-fillet margin on every side: D + 2 × 0.25)
parameters.who_else_asserted: The pre-2026-10-07 declared guess was 2.0 × 1.0 mm (2.5 × D) — a TODO(unverified) that would have been unsolderable, carried in the four committed footprint copies and docs/adr/045-*.md. Commit f89c3fa derives the 1.30 mm land from the operator-supplied 0.80 mm castellation datum (datasheet §9 'Mechanism Dimension' p8). The derivation, with the before/after table, is recorded in docs/f33-module/F33-LANDPATTERN-VERIFICATION.md §11.

exempt.reason: The land-pattern AUDIT record that documents the before/after ('before 2.0 × 1.0 mm' → 'after 1.30 × 1.30 mm', §11). It is the finding record; its '2.0 × 1.0' rows are the historical tables it exists to record.

forbid.note: asserts the F33 land is 2.0 × 1.0 mm (the old declared guess; now 1.30 × 1.30 mm derived from D)
